newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen lower, extends Mon. decline.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen lower, extends Mon. decline.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open lower Tuesday after finishing sharply lower yesterday on outlook of mild weather in the West and a slate of that region's power units back in service last weekend.
"They're falling hard," said a West Coast electricity dealer, adding over-the-counter (OTC) values continued yesterday's decline on the NYMEX in early trading.

NYMEX July California-Oregon Border (COB) futures, in OTC business, were quoted at $19.50-20.25 a megawatt hour (MWh), down from Monday's settlement at $21.10. July Palo Verde (PV) were assessed at $27.50-28.50, lower than yesterday's close at $30.57.
Firm, peak electricity prices at COB for Wednesday were assessed at $15.50-16.50, down from $19.00-20.00 for today, while those at PV at $28.00-31.00, lower than $42.00-43.00 for today.
The power complex was also under pressure Monday after Bonneville Power Administration slashed its next day peak firm power price by $12.00 per MWh to $19.00.

Two nuclear power units, the 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 1 and 1,221 MW Palo Verde 3, were boosting power early Tuesday following outages, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said in its daily plant status report.
A 750 MW unit at the Four Corners coal-fired plant in New Mexico was expected to restart at midnight Tuesday, slightly behind its original schedule.
Lower natural gas futures prices were also expected to exert downward pressure on power futures, market sources said.
NYMEX July Henry Hub natgas futures were down 1.5 cents at $2.095 per million British thermal units in early trading.

Temperatures in the West were called to average near to slightly above normal into early next week with above normal precipitation in the eastern sections of the Northwest and northern areas of the Southwest.
